name: teacher
description: Phase 3 — co-evolve the gaia-testbench benchmark so configs can't overfit a frozen dataset (PLAN.md §2e/§3.1, IMPLEMENTATION.md §2.8). Runs as a whole agent turn, slow-cron-fired. Flow: READ_STATE (find_blind_spots.py: where the top configs all pass = no signal, + the dataset-ideas queue) -> READ_IDEA/CLAIM (top unclaimed dataset idea, or autonomous harden) -> EVOLVE (prompt/output_schema: design ONE new held-out task aimed at a blind spot) -> WRITE_TASK (prompt/file-tools: write tasks/<id>.toml) -> APPLY (apply_dataset_evolution.py: validate via gaia get_task, append to benchmark-manifest, bump version, regen evaluate-config fan-out) -> RESCORE top-2 targets on the new version (command evaluate-config x2; held-out demotes overfits) -> SIGNAL/LOG. State on disk; a crash re-fires the cron. This is the anti-overfitting engine and the validity precondition for Phase-4 recursion.

read_state.name: READ_STATE
read_state.command:
set -eu
PY=/home/acer01/axi-assistant/.venv/bin/python
AR=/home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/autoresearch
SCRIPTS="$AR/dict/configs/optimizer-seed/scripts"
echo '=== BLIND-SPOT SCAN (top configs per-task discrimination; SATURATED = no signal) ==='
"$PY" "$SCRIPTS/find_blind_spots.py"
echo ''
echo '=== DATASET-IDEAS QUEUE (maintained by the dataset-secretary) ==='
grep -E '^- \[' "$AR/dataset-ideas.md" 2>/dev/null || echo '(no queued dataset ideas — harden a saturated task autonomously)'

read_idea.name: READ_DATASET_IDEA
read_idea.command:
set -eu
AR=/home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/autoresearch
IDEAS="$AR/dataset-ideas.md"
LINE=$(grep -m1 -E '^- \[ \] ' "$IDEAS" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -z "$LINE" ]; then echo 'dataset-auto-harden'; else echo "$LINE" | sed -E 's/^- \[ \] *//; s/:.*//'; fi

evolve.name: EVOLVE
evolve.prompt:
<sys>
You are the teacher for an autoresearch loop. Your job: design EXACTLY ONE new, harder / held-out gaia-testbench coding task that RESTORES DISCRIMINATION where the benchmark has gone flat — a task the current top configs would NOT all ace, so it separates good configs from better ones (PLAN.md §2e). This is the anti-overfitting engine.

Current benchmark state (blind-spot scan + the dataset-secretary's queued ideas):
{{benchmark_state}}

Guidance:
- Prefer the dataset idea '{{dataset_idea_id}}' if it names a concrete task; otherwise autonomously harden a SATURATED task (one every top config passes) — make a variant with an adversarial edge case, a stricter correctness bar, or a required verification step the easy version doesn't force.
- The task must be SELF-CONTAINED and run on a no-egress box: Python stdlib / provided files / shell only. No pip installs, no network. (gaia-testbench's own runnable tasks are all stdlib/tool-only.)
- It must have a DETERMINISTIC correctness oracle the judge can recompute by executing code (the judge can run Bash).
- task_id: a short kebab token, unique, not already in the benchmark; it becomes the tasks/<task_id>.toml filename stem (must match exactly).
- The three rubric criteria each tell the judge how to assign 1 (fails) / 2 (partial) / 3 (fully meets). 'verification' is judged from the tool-call trace only (did the agent test its own work?), the other two from the produced artifact.

Emit the task as structured output.
</sys>

task_id.description: kebab id == the tasks/<id>.toml filename stem; unique, not already in the benchmark

task_prompt.description: the coding task prompt handed to the agent-under-test; self-contained, stdlib/tool-only, deterministic oracle

correctness.description: rubric: how the judge assigns 1/2/3 for correctness, recomputable by running code

verification.description: rubric: how the judge assigns 1/2/3 for verification, judged from the tool-call trace only

code_quality.description: rubric: how the judge assigns 1/2/3 for code quality from the artifact

targets.description: which saturated task or dataset-idea this hardens, and why it discriminates

rationale.description: why the current top configs would NOT all pass this

write_task.name: WRITE_TASK
write_task.prompt:
<sys>
Write the new benchmark task to a TOML file, then stop. Change nothing else.

Write this EXACT file: /home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/soul-benchmarks/tasks/{{task_id}}.toml

Contents (use TOML triple-quoted '''...''' literals so no escaping is needed; the `id` MUST equal {{task_id}} exactly or gaia-testbench rejects the file):

  id = "{{task_id}}"
  prompt = '''<the task_prompt below, verbatim>'''
  notes = '''authored by teacher.json; targets: {{targets}}'''
  [rubric]
  correctness = '''<the correctness rubric below, verbatim>'''
  verification = '''<the verification rubric below, verbatim>'''
  code_quality = '''<the code_quality rubric below, verbatim>'''

Field values to insert verbatim:
- task_prompt: {{task_prompt}}
- correctness: {{correctness}}
- verification: {{verification}}
- code_quality: {{code_quality}}

Use the Write tool to create the file. If any field literally contains the sequence ''' , replace it with three single quotes spaced apart to keep the TOML valid. After writing, print 'wrote tasks/{{task_id}}.toml' and nothing else.
</sys>

signal.name: SIGNAL
signal.command:
set -eu
AR=/home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/autoresearch
echo "$(date +%FT%T) teacher done idea={{dataset_idea_id}} added={{task_id}} version={{new_version}}" >> "$AR/epoch-signals.log"
sed -i -E "s/^- \[~\] ({{dataset_idea_id}}:)/- [x] \1/" "$AR/dataset-ideas.md" 2>/dev/null || true
echo "signalled dataset-secretary: done {{dataset_idea_id}}"

log.name: LOG_TEACHER
log.command:
set -eu
AR=/home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/autoresearch
echo "$(date +%FT%T) teacher version={{new_version}} added={{task_id}} rescored={{topk_1}},{{topk_2}}" >> "$AR/teacher.log"
tail -1 "$AR/teacher.log"
